 Pakistan have booked their place in the final of the ACC Men’s U19 Asia Cup 2026, with India looking set to join them as they continue to dominate their semi-final clash against Afghanistan. Plenty of positives for Pakistan to take away from this game. They have fired on all cylinders, with their bowlers chipping in with wickets and their batters piling on the runs. Given their current form and momentum, they will certainly pose a strong challenge to India in what promises to be an exciting tournament final. Goodbye for now! Farhan Yousaf | Pakistan captain: I am very happy with the performance and it was a great effort from all guys. [On Hayam's inclusion] Yes, even in the last game, I was thinking about Hayam, but Jahangir is also a good player. So, for this match, I told the management that we should play Hayam. The management was very positive and supported my decision. Today, he played exceptionally well. [On their bowling performance] Yes, exactly. All the players are doing a great job. I especially want to mention my fielding unit. I think we have a fantastic fielding unit. All the bowlers are also doing a great job and hitting the right areas. That's why we are successful. [What will your message be to the team?] Just play your natural game and give 100%. Don't worry about the result. I believe that if we give 100%, the result doesn't matter. We will give our best, god has the best plan. Farid Hasan Faysal | Bangladesh captain: It just wasn't our day. We had a batting collapse, both in the top order and the middle order. So, it was a bad day for us. The Pakistani bowlers have been bowling really well throughout this tournament. Also, early in the morning, there was moisture on the pitch, which made it a very good time for bowling. [How would you sum up this campaign?] Reaching this stage is a confidence boost for my team. But today, unfortunately, it was just our bad luck. Rizwanullah: [Advice from the captain] The captain was saying that we just had to bowl wicket-to-wicket. That's exactly what I was doing, and it worked well. [On playing against UAE] Yes, it was my first match, so there was a little pressure. After that, our coaching staff told me not to worry about the pressure and just enjoy the game. [On the pitch] Yes, I was getting quite a lot of help. When I was bowling around the top of the stumps, the ball was getting some extra bounce. So I continued bowling in those areas, and the captain was also telling me to keep doing the same. [Preparations for the final] We'll have a simple plan. We'll do exactly what we've been doing in the previous matches. Rizwanullah is the Player of the Match 13:44 Local Time, 09:44 GMT, 15:14 IST: This was an easy chase. The Pakistan team were too hot to handle. They were the superior unit and chased this in a canter. Hayam Khan was brought into the XI today and he delivered as an aggressive opener. He took his chances and had his share of luck. But the intent was always there. Usman Khan also looked so promising and seemed like someone who knows his game. These are great signs for Pakistan as they have got some real firepower at the under-19 level. Some of them are very experienced at this level and that showed off as Bangladesh have been swatted away with elan. Barring the first couple of overs, nothing went right for the bowling side. There were half chances, dropped catches and some wayward bowling which added to their woes. Hang on for the presentation. 21.5 6 Rakibul Hossan to Usman Khan, SIX , just outside off, tossed up delivery, Usman Khan got under the ball and whacked it over deep mid. That was a towering blow from Usman Khan to finish it off. Pakistan win by 9 wickets and trample Bangladesh to make their way into their fifth final of the Asia Cup 21.4 4 Rakibul Hossan to Usman Khan, FOUR , tossed up delivery, outside off, Usman Khan gets under the ball and drills it over cover 21.3 Rakibul Hossan to Abdul Qadir, 1 run, tossed up delivery, driven down to long-on for a single 21.2 Rakibul Hossan to Abdul Qadir, no run, rippah of a leggie! That dipped, turned and beat the bat as Abdul Qadir wanted to push it and then was pegged back to see the ball turn away 21.1 6 Rakibul Hossan to Abdul Qadir, SIX , a little shimmy, got to the pitch of the ball and smoked it over long-off. That was a tossed up delivery and Abdul Qadir powered it over. He had some nets before this I guess Over 21 124-1 1 1 0 W 0 1 ( 3 runs) Abdul Qadir 1 (2) Usman Khan 54 (52) Robiul Hasan Anik 4-0-22-1 Over Summary View all overs 20.6 Robiul Hasan Anik to Abdul Qadir, 1 run, hangs back and pats it down to long-on for a single 20.5 Robiul Hasan Anik to Abdul Qadir, no run, tossed up delivery, Abdul Qadir gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it Abdul Qadir, right handed bat, comes to the crease 20.4 W Robiul Hasan Anik to Hayam Khan, out Caught by Farid Hasan Faysal!! Finally a wicket! The ball went off the edge as Hayam Khan tried to prod forward. The appeal was a generous one and the umpire took his time to give it out. Finally something for Bangladesh to rejoice. The break has helped. The keeper behind the sticks is still limping but he managed to hold on. Robiul Hasan Anik has delivered the breakthrough and Hayam Khan has finally run out of luck. Hayam Khan c Farid Hasan Faysal b Robiul Hasan Anik 69(72) [4s-8 6s-1] Robiul Hasan Anik to Hayam Khan, THATS OUT!! Caught!! 20.3 Robiul Hasan Anik to Hayam Khan, no run, dropped short, skidded on and Hayam Khan missed the pull. The keeper gets hit on the knees as the ball missed the padding. He is down writhing in pain. The physio is having a look 20.2 Robiul Hasan Anik to Usman Khan, 1 run, tossed up delivery, on the sticks, swept down to deep square for a single 20.1 Robiul Hasan Anik to Hayam Khan, 1 run, goes back and pats it down to long-on for a single Over 20 121-0 1 1 0 0 0 1 ( 3 runs) Hayam Khan 68 (69) Usman Khan 53 (51) Rakibul Hossan 2-0-14-0 Over Summary View all overs 19.6 Rakibul Hossan to Hayam Khan, 1 run, hangs back and punches the ball down to long-on for a single.
